body:
The issue seems to be that the shader is rendering an opaque quad over everything, and at certain angles, volumetric fog is appearing all black. So in that particular shader it looks like everything is getting cut off. But its just the volumetric fog being black

_Edit: The issue exists in 4.5 too. When turning away from DirectionalLights, volumetric fog has a very sharp cutoff in both 4.5 and 4.6. The difference between 4.5 and 4.6 is that 4.5 appears to retain the original surface color information better while in 4.6, the black volumetric fog appears to fully darken the quad. I am having trouble identifying what the correct behaviour should be in this case. The quad doesn't behave like actual geometry in the scene since it is pinned to the viewer's eye. The geometry used to calculate fog thus changes based on the direction of the camera and leads to some pretty weird positions._

_Further, I'm not certain what the intended purpose of the shader is. It seems very weird to display raw unlinearized depth combined with physically realistic volumetric fog. Ultimately, I'm not certain this is actually a bug. As far as I can tell the change in behaviour comes from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/112494. But I think the new behaviour is likely more correct. It would be interesting to see if there is an analogous issue in real scenes and what is going on there. But I think more likely than not, the old behaviour was a side effect of a bug in the Volumetric Fog blending code and was never intended._

_My gut feeling is that anyone doing the vertex shader trick to glue a quad to the viewer's eye in clip space should disable fog_

_Edit: oh, and for clarity, there is nothing wrong with the depth buffer in this scene. It is definitely not corrupted. The shader is just drawing over top of it_

> Ultimately, I'm not certain this is actually a bug. As far as I can tell the change in behaviour comes from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/112494. 

I can confirm that PR caused the issue.

> Further, I'm not certain what the intended purpose of the shader is. It seems very weird to display raw unlinearized depth combined with physically realistic volumetric fog. 

> My gut feeling is that anyone doing the vertex shader trick to glue a quad to the viewer's eye in clip space should disable fog

Sticking a QuadMesh onto the camera for screen space shaders is quite common as I'm sure you know. We've been using this method since Godot 3 days, and combined with volumetric fog since it became available in Godot 4, 4 years ago.

The purpose for the combination of screen space fog and volumetric fog is to be able to use fog volumes. Volumetric fog and regular godot fog don't look as good as our fog shader with our sky. In Out of the Ashes we use our screen space fog, and in swamp areas volumetric fog for a ground covering mist.

> But I think the new behaviour is likely more correct. It would be interesting to see if there is an analogous issue in real scenes and what is going on there. But I think more likely than not, the old behaviour was a side effect of a bug in the Volumetric Fog blending code and was never intended.

Real scenes are anyone using Sky3D or forks from the original, or anyone using a screen space shader and volumetric fog.

Shouldn't a screen space shader be able to render on top of anything the renderer outputs without conflicting?

If you're set on the idea that the current code is correct and the last several years was the wrong way, is there a way we can fix our shader? I'm open to tweaking it. But "don't use fog" or "rewrite the shader from scratch" aren't good options for such a long-standing use case.

I think the main question for me is why are you accumulating the Volumetric fog on the screen space quad?

This MRP calculates Volumetric fog twice for each pixel. First it calculates Volumetric Fog for each of the boxes that are drawn and for the sky. This looks totally correct and is functioning correctly. It then calculates Volumetric fog for the screen-covering quad as if it were an object in the scene and _adds_ that fog value on top of the existing fog. 

That second part is the part that doesn't make sense. The QuadMesh trick is indeed a common trick (I am the person who came up with it and documented it initially BTW), but it should be used to add a post processing to the screen. Treating it like a physical object in the scene doesn't make sense. That's why you always use `render_mode unshaded`, it doesn't make sense to add lighting to your full screen quad. It also doesn't make sense to add an extra pass of Volumetric Fog to it.


> Real scenes are anyone using Sky3D or forks from the original, or anyone using a screen space shader and volumetric fog.

No, you can easily have a screen space shader without running into this issue. The issue in this MRP is specifically caused by rendering an opaque mesh overtop of everything that accumulates Volumetric Fog. I.e. intentionally overwriting the existing screen color with color of the Volumetric fog

I found a suitable fix for the change in behaviour! 

So we can bring back the 4.5 behaviour without sacrificing the original fix. So my comments above are completely moot. I do question the correctness of applying Godot's volumetric fog to a screen-aligned quad. But if you are happy with the behaviour in 4.5, then it doesn't matter if it is correct or not.

Great news.

I don't understand what you mean by accumulating volumetric fog twice, or why you say we're using a shaded mesh, and an opaque quad. 

Our shader is marked unshaded. And we apply color with alpha transparency onto the camera feed. The original issue I reported on rocket chat and in #116038 is from Sky3D. 
https://github.com/TokisanGames/Sky3D/blob/main/addons/sky_3d/shaders/AtmFog.gdshader

> I do question the correctness of applying Godot's volumetric fog to a screen-aligned quad.

That sounds wasteful. But how are we doing that? We're rendering our own color, and applying that to albedo and alpha. Do you mean our depth calculations to create color, or are we doubling godot's world environment volumetric calculation somehow? 

I didn't make this issue or MRP. My issue had it's own trimmed down version of Sky3D for an MRP.

> That sounds wasteful. But how are we doing that? We're rendering our own color, and applying that to albedo and alpha. Do you mean our depth calculations to create color, or are we doubling godot's world environment volumetric calculation somehow?

Again, I haven't looked at your project. I have only looked at the MRP. The MRP is not using `render_mode fog_disabled`, so it is still calculating Volumetric Fog on the QuadMesh. Which indeed is doubling the volumetric fog calculation which is the core of this issue.

Lol, I added `fog_disabled` to our shader render_mode. It already has `unshaded`. That fixes the issue for 4.6-stable. No difference in performance, a very tiny visual difference, but our fog now works with volumetric fog and fog volumes once again. Thank you!
Amazing! I suspected that's the behaviour you wanted in the first place. At any rate, glad to hear that you can ship a quick fix without waiting for us to do a release.
